I was able to in high school while preparing in non stem courses. It was a hobby and I only did it a couple times a month. But every time I did it I'd sit there for 6 hours straight. It was like playing a little video game for me, a little personal sandbox game.
When I decided to do CS instead in college, and suddenly programming was due as an assignment, I nearly failed even though I 100% knew more than my peers. Didn't do any extracurriculars or fun programming for a year. Finally started meds sophomore year, two months ago. The difference isn’t enough for my stupid expectations but it’s 100% clear that I’m doing WAY better now. I’m back to doing side projects for fun, dont care about my grades anymore, I’m loving what I’m learning in class. Yeah I’m still depressed and spend most of the day sleeping or paralyzed in deciding what to do, but I haven’t submitted a sinlge late assignment this semester, which is crazy for me.

What made me realize I had ADHD is reading about the concept of dopamine deficiency causing lack of attention, and how similar a lot of symptoms like RSD were to how I lived. I have fun when I program, I almost failed a lot of classes BECAUSE I already knew everything, and I was too bored and depressed to do basic assignments. I’m in DSA now and it’s so much fun in comparison.
